meta.task: Price the short-lease discount from real quotes
meta.hard_rule: This dataset contains NO cap rates. Not one. No official federal, state or county source publishes single-tenant QSR cap rates, and this session did not obtain broker quotes. Every quote row is therefore null and flagged. Inventing a cap rate here would silently drive the entire sell-versus-hold answer, which is exactly the failure mode the owner asked to avoid.

why_this_matters: A short-lease discount is the gap between the cap rate a buyer pays for 15 years of remaining term and the cap rate they pay for 3-5 years. For single-tenant retail that gap is commonly several hundred basis points, but 'commonly' is not a quote. Because the discount multiplies directly into value, a 100 bp error on a 5% cap rate is roughly a 17% error in price.

quote_log.what: Broker opinion: cap rate for a freestanding QSR pad with 7+ years remaining
quote_log.why_missing: Not obtained. Requires a confidentiality agreement, a broker engaged under the owner's authority, and the parcel identity. Out of scope for a public repository.

quote_log.what: Broker opinion: cap rate for the same pad with 3-5 years remaining
quote_log.why_missing: Same as Q-01. This is the other end of the discount measurement.

quote_log.what: Comparable sale: QSR pad, central Los Angeles, closed in last 24 months
quote_log.source_type: county recorded deed grantee/grantor plus broker confirmation
quote_log.why_missing: Public recorded deeds give price but not NOI, so a cap rate cannot be derived from public records alone. Price-only comps are insufficient to price a discount.

quote_log.what: Comparable sale: QSR pad in the same submarket with similar remaining term
Lender quote: interest rate and LTV for a 5-year fixed loan on the asset
quote_log.why_missing: Needed to establish the spread over the 10-year Treasury anchor (VA-01 at 4.92%). Without it the hold-side refinancing assumption floats free.

quote_log.what: Insurance quote: annual premium for the building
quote_log.why_missing: Post-2025 fire market. Could plausibly move the hold case more than any rent assumption. Must not be estimated.

method_once_quotes_exist.step_1: Take the long-term cap rate from Q-01 and the short-term cap rate from Q-02 on the same asset, same submarket, same month. Any difference in asset quality invalidates the comparison.
method_once_quotes_exist.step_2: Short-lease discount = short-term cap rate minus long-term cap rate, in basis points.
method_once_quotes_exist.step_3: Value effect = NOI / long-term cap rate minus NOI / short-term cap rate. Report both the discount in bp and the value gap in dollars; they answer different questions.
method_once_quotes_exist.step_4: Sanity check against Q-03 and Q-04. If the broker-implied discount is not corroborated by at least one closed transaction or appraisal, treat it as an opinion and label it as such on the site.
method_once_quotes_exist.step_5: Back-test: apply the implied discount to three historical local sales if any can be documented, and show the error. Until step 5 can be run, the model stays labelled 'unbacktested'.
method_once_quotes_exist.anti_pattern: Do not average Q-01 and Q-02 into a single blended cap rate. The whole point is that they differ, and that difference is the priced risk.

what_the_public_record_does_show.what: Risk-free anchor available for spread construction
what_the_public_record_does_show.note: This is the only verified input on this page. Every cap-rate quote has to be expressed as a spread over it so the assumption is visible.

what_the_public_record_does_show.what: Local asset-price trend available for back-testing direction
what_the_public_record_does_show.note: Metro-wide and residential-weighted, so it cannot price a QSR pad. It can, however, be used to test whether a claimed appreciation rate is plausible.
